findings.text: RotoWire reports Week 5 Cowing 17 routes/50% of dropbacks and two targets; 92% of 11-personnel snaps but one of 25 in 12 personnel. Its last five table columns are season rates, distinct from the opening game-only columns. Counts are attributed to its NGS-based analysis, not independently recalculated.

FantasyPros cites Wicks' 17% target share in Weeks 1–3 with Smith, but warns of a likely third-option role with McKee. That conditional sample is more relevant than simply extrapolating Smith-absent targets, yet three games do not establish a stable forecast.
findings.confidence: MEDIUM for attribution; predictive effect untested

educational_lesson.central_method: Model personnel-conditioned route access separately from health clearance and target propensity.
educational_lesson.mathematics: Expected routes = sum over personnel groups of expected dropbacks in that group times conditional route participation. Expected targets require route-specific target propensity; snap share within a package is not itself route participation.
educational_lesson.synthetic_example: Invented teaching inputs, not player forecasts: 36 dropbacks, 40% in package A at 90% route participation and 60% in package B at 10% imply 15.12 routes. Raising A to 70% gives 23.76 routes without changing within-package ability. At assumed constant 20% target propensity these imply 3.024 versus 4.752 targets.
limitations: Real personnel selection and pass probability are dependent.
Injury replacement may change package mix and within-package role simultaneously.
One observed game or full practice cannot estimate stable conditional rates.

research_proposals.name: Personnel-conditioned role forecasts outperform unconditional last-game route share
research_proposals.testing_method: Freeze both methods before kickoff on identical receiver candidates. Fit on earlier weeks, test later weeks, retain inactive/zero-route cases, and compare route MAE, target MAE and interval coverage with game-clustered uncertainty.
research_proposals.failure_condition: Reject if held-out gains disappear after zero-route cases or injury-driven mix changes are retained.
